# Hosea Chapter 7 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folio 331v | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/HOS_007_page_001.jpg

---

**7:4** All-of-them [kullam] [are] adulterers [mena'afim]; like an-oven [tannur] burning [bo'arah] from-a-baker [me-ofeh]; he-ceases [yishbot] from-stirring [me'ir] from-kneading [mi-lush] of-dough [batseq] until it-is-leavened [chumtso].

**7:8** Efrayim — among-the-nations he-mixes-himself [yitbolal]; Efrayim is a-cake [ugah] not-turned [beli hafukhah].

**7:11** And-Efrayim is like-a-dove [ke-yonah] — silly [potah], without [ein] heart [lev]; Mitsrayim they-call [qare'u], to-Ashur they-go [halakhu].

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

**v.8 — "a cake not turned":** One of Hosea's most vivid metaphors — Ephraim is a flatbread baked on one side only, burned on the bottom and raw on top. Half-baked religion, half-baked politics, half-baked loyalty.

**v.11 — "a silly dove":** Ephraim flutters between Egypt and Assyria for political alliances, unable to commit. The image of a witless pigeon captures political vacillation perfectly.

*— EMET*
